design.text: Prospective, single-center, single-dose, single-arm, non-comparative study assessing imaging performance of Cu-64 dotatate PET by comparison of blinded PET reader results to a standard of truth (SOT).

citations.quote: Study RMX-18-22 was a phase 3, prospective, single-center (Excel Diagnostics and Nuclear Oncology Center in Houston), single-dose, single-arm, non-comparative clinical study.
The primary objective of the study was to assess the imaging performance of Cu-64 dotatate PET through comparison of individual PET reader results to a SOT for each subject.

endpoint.text: Co-primary endpoints: subject-level sensitivity and specificity of Cu-64 dotatate PET for NET, assessed against a standard of truth (SOT).

result.text: All three blinded readers demonstrated success on the co-primary efficacy endpoints, with lower bounds of the 95% CI for PPA (sensitivity) exceeding 70% and NPA (specificity) exceeding 60%. PPA (sensitivity) was 91% for all three readers and NPA (specificity) ranged from 80 to 97%.

citations.quote: All three readers demonstrated success on the co-primary efficacy endpoints with their lower bounds of the 95% CI for PPA (sensitivity) exceeding 70% and NPA (specificity) exceeding 60%.
The PPA was 91% for all three readers, and the NPA ranged from 80 to 97% for the three readers.

indication.text: Detectnet is a radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for use with positron emission tomography (PET) for localization of somatostatin receptor positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in adult patients.

citations.quote: Detectnet is a radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for use with positron emission tomography (PET) for localization of somatostatin receptor positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in adult patients. (1)

target_moa.text: Copper Cu 64 dotatate binds to somatostatin receptors (highest affinity for SSTR2); the somatostatin analog octreotate binds SSTRs, DOTA is the chelator, and Cu-64 is the positron emitter, so PET images indicate the presence and density of somatostatin receptors in tissues.

citations.quote: Copper Cu 64 dotatate binds to somatostatin receptors. Based upon the intensity of the signals, PET images obtained using copper Cu 64 dotatate injection indicate the presence and density of somatostatin receptors in tissues.
The Cu-64 dotatate molecule has three regions, namely the somatostatin analog octreotate, the chemical linker tetrexetan (DOTA) and the positron emitter Cu-64.
Cu-64 dotatate binds to SSTRs with highest affinity for SSTR2.

modality.text: Radiopharmaceutical (Cu-64 radiolabeled somatostatin analog peptide for PET imaging)

citations.quote: RadioMedix has developed copper Cu 64 dotatate injection (hereafter referred to as Cu-64 dotatate) as a radioactive diagnostic agent for use with positron emission tomography (PET) of somatostatin receptor (SSTR) positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in adults.

summary.text: Detectnet was submitted as a 505(b)(2) NDA for a designated new molecular entity and reviewed under Priority review. It received Fast Track designation (December 19, 2018) and orphan drug designation (May 18, 2016) as a diagnostic for the management of NETs; because of the orphan designation, PREA pediatric requirements were not applicable. It was approved on the standard (non-accelerated) pathway.

citations.quote: New drug application (NDA) 213227 is a 505(b)(2) application for this designated new molecular entity (NME).
Under IND 131797, Fast Track designation was granted for this product on December 19, 2018.

On May 18, 2016, orphan drug designation was granted to Cu-64 dotatate as a diagnostic for the management of NETs. Therefore, Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) requirements are not applicable to this NDA.
